title: We Lift Our Hearts to Thee
description: We Lift Our Hearts to Thee in Tonic Solfa to AYLESBURY, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. They were printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 25.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to AYLESBURY; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: We lift our hearts to Thee, O Day star from on high! The sun it-self is but Thy shade, Yet cheers both earth and sky.

lines: We lift our hearts to Thee,
The sun itself is but Thy shade,
Yet cheers both earth and sky.
The mists of error and of vice,
With joy we view the pleasing change
May Jesus’ blood, like morning dew,
And live this short, revolving day
As if it were our last.

licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to AYLESBURY by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
